claims.statement: Endpoint differences telescope to zero on a declared directed closed walk, hence C(h-df)=C(h). For the rational triangle, df=(1/3,1/3,-2/3) and residual=(0,0,1); a constant potential shift changes neither. A zero sum suffices for a potential on the single cycle by successive partial sums.
claims.limits: Algebraic derivation under explicit orientation/coefficients; finite tests instantiate it. No quotient optimum, physical interpretation, learner gain or arbitrary-graph sufficiency inferred.

claims.statement: A reversed difference convention also telescopes to zero and preserves the residual sum, so aggregate cycle-sum assertions accept this wrong-sign mutant. Independently computed coordinate checks distinguish it; equality of LP objectives similarly needs feasibility before serving as a certificate.
claims.limits: Demonstrates specific finite checker weaknesses, not complete adversarial robustness or sufficiency of all existing checkers.
